summary:
This is the opening page of **chapter 3, "Introduction to TensorFlow, PyTorch, JAX, and Keras"** (PDF pp.84-127).

The *This chapter covers* box lists two goals:

- a closer look at all major deep learning frameworks and their relationships;
- an overview of how core deep learning concepts translate to code across all frameworks.

The introduction says the chapter is meant to give you everything you need to start doing deep learning in practice. First you get familiar with three popular frameworks that can be used with Keras: **TensorFlow** (tensorflow.org), **PyTorch** (pytorch.org) and **JAX** (jax.readthedocs.io). Then, building on the first contact with Keras in chapter 2, the chapter reviews the core components of neural networks and how they translate to Keras APIs. By the end you should be ready for practical, real-world applications, which start in chapter 4.

According to the chapter outline, the sections are: 3.1 a brief history of deep learning frameworks (p.85); 3.2 how these frameworks relate to each other (p.87); 3.3 TensorFlow, 3.4 PyTorch and 3.5 JAX, each with first steps, an end-to-end linear classifier written in that framework alone, and what makes its approach unique (pp.87-114); and 3.6 Keras (p.114), covering layers, models, the compile step, loss functions, fit(), validation monitoring and inference.

**How to use this page:** treat it as a map. If you already know one framework, the parallel structure of sections 3.3-3.5 (the same linear classifier in each) makes them easy to compare side by side.

paragraphs.excerpt: This chapter is meant to give you everything you need to start
paragraphs.what_it_says: The chapter aims to give you everything needed to start doing deep learning in practice, beginning with three popular frameworks usable with Keras: TensorFlow, PyTorch and JAX.
paragraphs.what_it_means: In chapter 2 Keras was used as a black box and the from-scratch code borrowed TensorFlow's GradientTape (p.80). Here the underlying frameworks become explicit subjects. Keras 3 runs on top of any of the three, so learning them clarifies what Keras is doing underneath.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Knowing the backends lets you read code written directly in them and choose the right one for a project.

concepts.name: Deep learning framework
concepts.definition: A software library (TensorFlow, PyTorch, JAX) for tensor computation with automatic differentiation and hardware acceleration; Keras is a higher-level API that can run on any of them.
concepts.intuition: The engine underneath; Keras is the dashboard.
concepts.technical: Section 3.1 lists three key features: autodiff, running tensor computations on CPUs and GPUs, and distributing computation across devices (p.85).
concepts.significance: Every model in the rest of the book runs on one of these frameworks.
concepts.example: The from-scratch MNIST code used TensorFlow's GradientTape for gradients (p.80).
concepts.misconception: Keras is not a competitor to these frameworks in the same layer; in Keras 3 it sits on top of them.

questions.question: Before reading on, can you name the components of a training setup from chapter 2 that you expect to see as Keras APIs (e.g. layers, model, loss, optimizer, training loop)?
questions.answer: Layers (Dense), a model chaining them, a loss, an optimizer, the fit loop, evaluation and prediction.
questions.explanation: Section 3.6 covers layers, models, compile (loss, optimizer, metrics), fit, validation and inference, mirroring the from-scratch pieces of pp.77-82.

questions.question: Why might it help to learn TensorFlow, PyTorch and JAX if you will mostly write Keras code?
questions.answer: Because Keras runs on top of them; understanding the backend clarifies what Keras does underneath, lets you read code written directly in those frameworks, and helps you choose a backend.
questions.explanation: The chapter frames the frameworks as things that 'can be used with Keras', and chapter 2 already relied on TensorFlow's autodiff (p.80). The benefits listed are an inference from that framing.

questions.question: In which chapter does the book say practical, real-world applications begin?
questions.explanation: The last sentence of the page says so.
